claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation at 300–500°C under controlled oxygen partial pressure and dwell time will form a uniform nanocrystalline oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu.
The pre-formed oxide layer may have a spinel structure.
The nanocrystalline oxide layer will act as a load-bearing protective barrier.
The oxide layer will provide a self-lubricating or lubricious interface.
The lubricious oxide interface will reduce friction at high temperature.
The load-bearing oxide barrier will reduce wear at high temperature.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have significantly lower friction coefficients than untreated coatings.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower wear-track depth than untreated coatings.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower wear volume than untreated coatings.
Pre-oxidation will enhance the overall high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
The beneficial effect will be observable only at 200–500°C under high-loading conditions.
At temperatures below 200°C, the benefits of the pre-formed oxide may be negligible.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify temperatures above 200°C, whereas the boundary and experiment include 200°C. This creates a minor ambiguity over whether the lower boundary is inclusive.
